summary: Verdantis Pharmaceuticals - priority request queue saturation causing 5xxs and tail latency; customer escalation and post-incident playbook
description:
Issue summary:
Verdantis observed sustained 5xx responses and severe long-tail latency for enterprise-priority requests beginning 2026-03-05 02:08 UTC. Traffic was hitting 'redwood-3b-quantized' in us-east-1 and requests backlogged in the priority queue, triggering customer escalation to Support and SRE. Impact: production request failures for Verdantis clinical ingestion pipeline (batch + realtime), resulting in downstream job failures and temporary SLA breach.

Impact:
- ~12% of Verdantis production requests returned 5xx between 02:08–03:10 UTC.
- Median latency for priority requests rose from ~70ms to 1.8s; 99th percentile > 12s.
- Customer reported 3 downstream job aborts and manual intervention.
- Billing exposure: invoices could reflect retries and failed completions; finance requested an estimate of charged tokens.

Environment:
- prod (us-east-1); customer uses enterprise plan with reserved capacity + priority routing.
- Serving runtime: redwood-3b-quantized on GPU pool rp-us-east-priority-01.

Timeline (high level):
- 02:08 UTC: Verdantis CSM reported increased 5xx via #support channel.
- 02:12 UTC: SRE on-call acknowledged and opened incident bridge.
- 02:20–02:35 UTC: Observed queue depth spike on rp-us-east-priority-01 and increased request retries.
- 02:36 UTC: Autoscaler failed to add new capacity (pods in Pending for >90s).
- 02:50 UTC: Engineering applied routing override to send priority traffic to rp-us-east-burst-01; immediate reduction in 5xx.
- 03:05 UTC: Temporary mitigation fully in place; customer traffic normalized.
- 03:10–03:30 UTC: Post-incident monitoring and validation.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Simulate synthetic priority traffic matching Verdantis request size/sequence distribution (long upfront prefixes + embeddings calls).
2) Force a small-scale autoscaler delay (e.g., increase pod startup simulated + cloud preemption).
3) Observe queue depth growth and 5xx generation once queue threshold exceeded.

Logs & telemetry pointers:
- Metrics dashboards: /dashboards/priority-queue-us-east (link in Confluence page).
- Error logs: serving-runtime/error.log timestamps 2026-03-05T02:20:xx showing 'queue_deadline_exceeded' and 'failed_dispatch: 502'.
- Autoscaler events: k8s events show 'FailedScheduling' due to node resource contention from nvidia-driver update.

Immediate mitigation applied:
- Traffic rerouted to secondary burst pool (rp-us-east-burst-01) and fallback routing rules tightened.
- Increased ephemeral reserved capacity by 2x for Verdantis for 1 hour.
- Issued customer communication explaining temporary mitigations and crediting plan for disruption.

Root cause (summary):
- Primary cause: scheduler/routing policy misclassification that allowed priority requests to remain tied to a single drainable GPU pool during a simultaneous node driver update. The autoscaler experienced elevated pod Pending time because new nodes were slow to come up (image + driver init), allowing queue depth to exceed the queue_deadline threshold and generate 502s.
- Contributing factors: lack of a circuit-breaker on queue-length per-customer, insufficient autoscaler warmup heuristics for reserved priority pools, and no automatic pre-warm on planned driver maintenance windows.

Resolution and customer remediation:
- Rollout of temporary routing override and capacity bump restored service.
- Applied k8s affinity tweak to prefer stable nodes for priority pools and adjusted autoscaler warmup target from 90s to 45s for reserved pools.
- Billing: finance will compute credits for Verdantis for failed requests and retries; Support will confirm once calculation complete.

Follow-up action items (owners & due dates):
- SRE (Priya Patel): implement per-customer queue-length circuit breaker and alert (due 2026-03-19).
- Infra (Diego Morales): add autoscaler warmup configuration and pre-warm hook for scheduled node image updates (due 2026-03-22).
- Platform (Lena Wu): add canary to routing policy changes and add test that simulates priority-pool drain (due 2026-03-26).
- Customer Success (Amir Ghose): confirm credit amount with finance and communicate to Verdantis (due 2026-03-10 - completed).

Notes: incident postmortem draft is on Confluence; small code change landed in runtime to expose queue length per-customer (PR linked).
